content_html_sanitized:
Last September, I wrote a column, Cannabis and Democracy: Who Are Our Leaders Following? It Ain't Us!, about the puzzling phenomenon of politicians opposing something that is overwhelmingly popular like medical cannabis.

 

For professional Prohibitionists, it can make perfect sense, because there’s a lot of money in losing. It’s called repeat business.

See

President Trump May Or May Not Be About To Reschedule Marijuana But Don’t Question Kevin Sabet’s Motives Or His Lawyer Will Want Your Address (Especially If You Live In Hungary!)

Now See

Sabet Hires Bill Barr To Try And Reverse DOJ Cannabis Scheduling Process As & When It Happens

“A leading marijuana prohibitionist group says it’s retained the legal services of President Donald Trump’s former attorney general, Bill Barr, to sue to reverse federal marijuana rescheduling if and when the pending rule is finalized. And they’ll also be filing a petition through the administrative process to keep cannabis strictly prohibited.”  Barr reminds me of a villain from  Star Wars, only meaner.

 

Nonetheless, Republican Politicians who are usually afraid to oppose President Trump on any issue, are lining up to oppose the rescheduling of Marijuana. They are even claiming that Chinese Communist gangs are taking over medical marijuana businesses in Maine. Yeah, just like Al Capone took over the alcohol business AFTER alcohol Prohibition was Repealed??

 

The White House has taken a very moderate approach.

https://www.whitehouse.gov

INCREASING MEDICAL MARIJUANA AND CANNABIDIOL RESEARCH – The ...

18 Dec 2025 — “One patient survey showed that just 56 percent of older Americans using marijuana have discussed the usage with their healthcare provider. This places patients, especially seniors who may be on multiple medications, at increased risk of drug interactions or other adverse events.”

 

That is a very straightforward argument for reclassifying marijuana,  for medical purposes that would not cause teenagers to want to light up.

 

And from MarijuanaMoment.net

See 9 In 10 Americans Support Legalizing Marijuana In Some Form, Including Bipartisan Majorities, Pew Poll Shows

8 Jul 2025 — Fifty-four percent said marijuana should be legal for both medical and recreational purposes, while 33 percent said it should be exclusively ...nearly nine in 10—support legalizing marijuana in some form, according to newly released polling data from the Pew Research Center. Asked about cannabis policy preferences, 87 percent of respondents said they agreed with enacting reform. Fifty-four percent said marijuana should be legal for both medical and recreational purposes, while 33 percent said it should be exclusively legal for medical use. Only 12 percent of U.S. adults think cannabis should remain prohibited across the board.”

And yet???

 

Meanwhile, in Maine and Massachusetts, the Prohibitionists have managed to get initiatives on this fall’s ballot to recriminalize possession. The Massachusetts initiative seems certain to fail. Maine is a bit more complicated.

 

However, Massachusetts is about to do something very important, and allow the equivalent of Dutch “coffee shops.”

See

Meanwhile Back In Amsterdam: The Fiftieth Anniversary Of The Bulldog, The First “CoffeeShop”

See

Cannabis Control Commission Massachusetts

https://masscannabiscontrol.com

Massachusetts Social Consumption Establishment Regulations are Now in Effect

 

Don’t light up yet. January 2, 2026 — “The Secretary of the Commonwealth promulgated new regulations that will allow the on-site consumption of cannabis at licensed Social Consumption venues.”

 

“Although the regulations take effect immediately, social consumption licenses are not yet available, and businesses will not be authorized to sell regulated cannabis to consumers for on-site consumption until receiving a state license to do so. Over the next several months….”

 

The Boston area has some of the leading universities in the world, and the cannabis community needs to develop more than just a replica of the Dutch coffee shops, which have been operating in a tolerant environment. In our world, it needs to develop the equivalent of  the English Coffee Houses of the 17th and 18th Centuries, political and social venues.

 

Of course, the same would apply for every campus in the country. As long as the legal age is 21, which is absurd, the Cannabis Coffee Houses will be for Seniors, which may actually work to our advantage politically.

 

The last two rights listed in the First Amendment are “the freedom of assembly, or the right to petition the government for redress of grievances.”

 

It is difficult to think of two rights that apply more strongly to cannabis than these two, and especially in the present context.

Marijuananews note:

Marijuana Social Clubs Are The Last Major Step for Legalization

And

Cannabis Prohibition: The Longest Lockdown. Social Isolation Is Harmful For Everyone

 

We need to use our First Amendment rights to demand that we have the right of Assembly in our coffeehouses and use them as bases for organizing. It is quite clear that the Prohibitionists will never quit, so we cannot. Eternal Vigilance!
